open_points.subject: Customer-value collection in mapping input
open_points.text: "keyed by that v1 value: at most one entry for each v1 value" and "one given twice too (`duplicate_pick`)"
open_points.question: Must the operation receive a duplicate-preserving sequence of Customer-value entries so it can detect repeated v1 values, or a keyed collection in which duplicates cannot exist?
options: A duplicate-preserving list is accepted as input and repeated keys produce `duplicate_pick`.
A keyed map is accepted and duplicate detection happens before this operation.
A keyed map is accepted and duplicate keys are resolved rather than refused.
open_points.default_guess: Use a duplicate-preserving list and have this operation return `duplicate_pick`.

witness.initial: The uploaded file contains picked projects that name v1 customer value `C1`.
events: The owner submits mapping values containing two entries keyed by `C1`.
outcomes: The input preserves both entries and the operation refuses with `invalid_request` / `duplicate_pick`.
The input is a keyed map, so one entry overwrites the other or the caller rejects it before this operation.
witness.observer: The owner and the `operations` module see different refusal ownership and results.

open_points.subject: Default display name and alias for a picked project
open_points.text: The input requires picks "each with the display name and alias it arrives under", while A16 says it arrives under "its v1 name and no alias unless the owner gives others".
open_points.question: When the owner picks a project without supplying a name or alias override, does this operation derive the v1 name and absent alias, require `operations` to supply those effective values, or report them as missing?
options: The operation derives the v1 display name and absent alias when overrides are omitted.
`operations` must supply the effective v1 name and absent alias in every pick.
An omitted display name or alias is reported as a missing mapping value.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the submitted values as optional overrides and derive the v1 name and no alias when omitted.

witness.initial: An accepted upload contains project `P1` with v1 name `Reforma Norte`; the owner wants to keep that name and give no alias.
events: The owner selects `P1` without entering either override.
outcomes: The mapping shows `P1` arriving as `Reforma Norte` with no alias and may be clean.
The mapping reports a missing value, or the call cannot be made until `operations` manufactures and supplies the defaults.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the project can be confirmed without re-entering its existing name.

open_points.subject: Customer details in the mapping output
open_points.text: The output says "the Customers it will make by their v1 value with the projects each links" but does not say whether it returns the supplied Customer name, kind and tax-id choice.
open_points.question: Does each Customer in the mapping output include the exact name, kind and tax-id choice that will be bound to confirmation, or only its v1 value and linked projects?
options: Return the v1 value, linked projects, name, kind and tax-id choice.
Return only the v1 value and linked projects; the owner interface must merge the submitted values itself.
Return supplied values only when they are missing or invalid.
open_points.default_guess: Return all supplied Customer values alongside the v1 value and linked projects.

events: The owner supplies customer name `Empresa Uno`, kind `company`, and says `C1` is its tax id.
`read_import_mapping` returns a clean mapping for the confirmation page.
outcomes: The returned Customer item includes `Empresa Uno`, `company` and the affirmative tax-id choice.
The returned item contains only `C1` and its link to `P1`; the owner interface must recover the other values from the request.
witness.observer: The owner interface implementer and the owner see whether the confirmed Customer values come from the mapping answer.

open_points.subject: Order of projects in upload-mode output
open_points.text: "At `upload`, each project the file holds with its id and status."
open_points.question: In what order must upload mode return the projects: by `project_id`, in file order, or another declared order?
options: Sort by `project_id`, as the import mapping's projects are ordered by A06 rule 8.
Preserve the projects' order in the export file.

witness.initial: The file contains project `B` before project `A`.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different project-selection order, and contract tests observe different arrays.

open_points.subject: Record position reported by mapping defects
open_points.text: A record is named by "its position among the file's records of that kind".
open_points.question: Is the reported position zero-based or one-based, and is it the position in the original file rather than in a filtered collection of picked records?
options: Use a zero-based position in the original sequence of records of that kind.
Use a one-based position in the original sequence of records of that kind.
Use the position after filtering records to the selected projects.
open_points.default_guess: Use a zero-based position in the original sequence of records of that kind.

witness.initial: The first room record in the file is malformed and belongs to a picked project.
events: `read_import_mapping` names the malformed room by its position.
outcomes: The defect identifies the room at position `0`.
The defect identifies the same room at position `1`.
witness.observer: The owner interface, diagnostics shown to the owner, and contract tests see different position values.
